subject: Crestline renewal: step-up rate band + credit structure
messages:
From: Becca Nolan <becca@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity growth and pricing question

Rishi,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're coming up on our July renewal (current term ends 2027-07-15) and I wanted to start the pricing conversation early. Usage at Crestline has grown ~2.6x since last year—our ML team is ramping more models and the infra spend is a material line item.

Quick context:
- Current committed capacity: 40K token-hrs/month (annual commitment)
- Projected consumption through year 1 of the renewal: ~95K token-hrs/month (peak)
- Primary ask: a predictable price path (we prefer a 12-18 month window) and something that gives us room to scale without 3x overage shock

Can Redwood provide: a step-up commit structure we can align to (so we start smaller and step to commitments as we scale), any short-term price-hold during an initial onboarding window, and confirmation on what onboarding/early-month credits you can offer to offset migration friction? Procurement will likely ask for a sample amendment to review with legal — happy to set a time for a call.

Thanks,
Becca Nolan
Head of ML Platforms, Crestline Health
[phone redacted]

[External Attachment: Crestline_usage_export_Q1.csv (CSV, 220 KB)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Becca Nolan <becca@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Alan Torres <alan.torres@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity growth and pricing question

Becca — really appreciate the visibility. Congratulations on the growth — exciting!

High level proposal (initial):
- Term: 12 months with automated step-ups at month 4 and month 8 (3-step band): 50K -> 80K -> 120K token-hrs/month committed.
- Unit price: tiered rate table (attached) with a 6-month price-hold on the blended unit price for the lower two bands; step to the top band triggers a 90-day notice before full rate change.
- Credits: one-time migration credit equal to 10% of Q1 projected invoice (applied as dollar credits across first 3 invoices). We are willing to allocate an additional onboarding support credit of up to $15,000 if Crestline signs within 30 days.
- Overage: burst pool with capped per-token rate (we can cap the overage multiplier at 1.6x the committed rate during the first 90 days post-step).
- Ops: Dedicated onboarding task force and two weeks of prioritized support during model migration windows.

I've attached a short summary and a tracked-diff amendment that Procurement can review; this is intentionally conservative on concessions and preserves SLA language for the Dedicated tier you mentioned previously. If that looks OK, can we book a 30-minute call this week to walk legal/procurement through the amendment?

Attachments: [Crestline_Renewal_Summary_v1.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)] [proposed-amendment-diff.docx (DOCX, 45 KB)]

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T14:44:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Crestline renewal — pricing and credit thinking (internal)

Thanks for the draft Rishi — digging in. A couple of internal points before we go live: 

1) Credits: 10% migration credit + $15k onboarding is generous for a first-pass. Recommend we cap onboarding support credit to $10k and make the additional $5k conditional on hitting the step to 80K within 90 days.
2) Price-hold: 6 months is fine, but the blended unit price math is sensitive. Let's include language that the hold applies only to "committed-unit blended rate" and excludes accumulated overage multipliers. 
3) Overage cap at 1.6x is OK short-term, but let's put an explicit annual true-up clause that triggers if cumulative consumption exceeds 2.8x baseline consumption — this will protect unit economics.
4) Step schedule: can we make the month-8 step opt-in with a 30-day notification from Crestline to avoid forcing them into a rate change if they choose to remain at a lower commit?

I'll mark up the amendment with these changes. If Marissa agrees, we can present a revised proposal with the reduced onboarding credit and explicit true-up clause.

Ben
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-04-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Crestline renewal — pricing and credit thinking (internal)

Ben — agree with tightening the onboarding credit. Suggest a compromise that keeps the headline concession attractive to the customer while protecting margin:

- Keep the 10% migration credit applied as Rishi proposed.
- Onboarding support credit: $10k guaranteed + additional $5k performance credit that vests upon 60-day milestone (reach 75% of the 80K step average for any 30-day window).
- Make the month-8 step opt-in as Ben suggested, but offer a one-time startup bump (a single month of grace on overage multiplier at 1.2x) if they provide notice within the 30-day window and commit to the opt-in.
- Replace the "annual true-up" wording with a clear, mutual measurement: a 12-month consumption true-up that only applies if cumulative consumption > 3x prior baseline; calculations use the signed usage export as baseline with a mutually agreed lookback period.

I'll attach a short deal worksheet showing expected retention impact and a templated DocuSign amendment with the tiered language. We should present this on the call as "A-B compromise" — externally it reads as a simple step-up + short-term credit, internally it preserves our protections.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Pricing | Redwood Inference

Becca / Alan / procurement team — thanks for the productive conversation last week. Per our call and internal alignment, below is the agreed commercial point summary. I attached the redline we signed off on internally and a clean amendment for your legal/procurement review.

Agreed commercial summary:
- Term: 12 months starting 2027-07-15.
- Commit bands (monthly token-hrs): 50,000 (initial) -> 80,000 (month 4 opt-in) -> 120,000 (month 8 opt-in). Opt-in must be provided 30 days before the scheduled step.
- Unit price: tiered discounted rates per band (see attached amendment). 6-month price-hold applies to the committed blended unit rate for the initial band; price changes for step-ups follow the amendment notice cadence.
- Credits: 10% migration credit applied across first three invoices. Onboarding support credit: $10,000 guaranteed + $5,000 performance credit tied to 60-day uptake milestone (reach 75% of the 80K step rolling 30-day avg).
- Overage/burst policy: burst pool with capped multiplier (1.6x) for first 90 days after stepping; single-month grace at 1.2x if Crestline provides timely opt-in notice when electing month-8 step.
- True-up: 12-month cumulative true-up applies only if annualized consumption exceeds 3x the signed baseline.
- SLA/ops: Dedicated onboarding task force and two weeks of prioritized migration support.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached clean amendment. If acceptable, sign via DocuSign within 30 days to lock in the onboarding credit. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/sign/ABC123def456
2) Once signed, we will schedule the onboarding kickoff and assign the task force.
3) Rishi will send a pre-kickoff checklist and an ops contact list.
